QUOTE: "If any of the remaining kinds (typedefs, macros, variables, and so on) hold a row matching the query, the reply says "NOT DEFINITIVE — this index HOLDS matching rows that search does not read"... The check is derived by subtraction, so a new kind downgrades the verdict without an edit to the emptiness code."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the verdict is computed per query by checking which kinds the index holds that search did not read (`unsearched_corpora`), and the strong "definitive" wording is granted only when that check finds nothing, instead of being tied to the shape of the result.
